chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Mihran ibn Muhammad, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: When the deceased dies, Allah sends an angel to the most pained one of his family, and he wipes upon his heart, causing him to forget the anguish of grief; and had it not for that, the world would not be inhabited.

key_terms.أَوْجَعِ أَهْلِهِ: the most pained one of his family
key_terms.فَمَسَحَ عَلَى قَلْبِهِ: and he wiped upon his heart

ai.seo_question: How does Allah comfort the grieving family of the deceased according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kulayni’s *al-Kafi*, this hadith highlights the divine mercy (*rahma*) that prevents grief from becoming a paralyzing force, ensuring the continuity of human life and societal stability. The specific mention of the 'most grieving' individual underscores the psychological reality that intense sorrow is a natural, divinely ordained experience rather than a spiritual failure, a concept often discussed in Shia tafsir regarding the patience of the Ahl al-Bayt.
